$comment: GnuCOBOL 3.2 (`cobc`; DESIGN-conformance-suite.md §5). -std selects the dialect's warnings and features: it is
the flag-mode, not a conformance mode, and there is no 2023 dialect, so the 2023 suite is NOT APPLICABLE.
cobc refuses a source file base name longer than 31 characters ('invalid file base name ... length exceeds
maximum', measured on 3.2.0), so the harness names the source within that limit. A diagnostic reads
`<file>:<line>: error|warning: ...`; a line naming another file (`<command-line>`, a copybook) is not the
test's. An ASSIGN name is a file of the working directory (cobc also maps DD_<name>, dd_<name> and <name>
environment variables, none of which the harness sets). Run it where cobc is: on Windows, under WSL.
